name: FTC

summary.text: The Federal Trade Commission is the U.S. consumer-protection and competition agency. On this site it appears through the Cambridge Analytica affair: on July 24, 2019 it announced a $5 billion civil penalty and new privacy governance requirements for Facebook to settle charges that the company violated a 2012 FTC order, and in the same month it filed an administrative complaint against Cambridge Analytica and settled with the firm's former chief executive Alexander Nix and app developer Aleksandr Kogan. The Commission issued an opinion and final order against Cambridge Analytica in late 2019 and gave final approval to the Nix and Kogan settlements in December 2019.

facts.claim: On July 24, 2019 the FTC announced that Facebook would pay a $5 billion penalty, described by the agency as the largest ever imposed on any company for violating consumers' privacy, to settle charges that it violated a 2012 FTC order by deceiving users about their ability to control the privacy of their personal information. The order also required new privacy governance mechanisms intended to hold Facebook executives accountable for privacy decisions.
facts.quote: The $5 billion penalty against Facebook is the largest ever imposed on any company for violating consumers' privacy

sources.title: FTC Imposes $5 Billion Penalty and Sweeping New Privacy Restrictions on Facebook
FTC's $5 billion Facebook settlement: Record-breaking and history-making

facts.claim: FTC Chairman Joe Simons said at the July 24, 2019 press conference that the $5 billion penalty was about 9% of Facebook's 2018 revenue and about 23% of its 2018 profit. The Commission's vote was 3-2, with two commissioners saying they would have preferred litigation to seek tougher penalties; Facebook did not admit wrongdoing.
facts.quote: two of the five commissioners opposing the settlement and saying they would have preferred litigation to seek tougher penalties

sources.title: Remarks of Chairman Joe Simons, Facebook press conference
FTC fines Facebook $5B, adds limited oversight on privacy

facts.claim: In April 2020 the FTC gave final approval to modifying its 2012 privacy order with Facebook to include the provisions of the 2019 settlement. Facebook's 2021 Form 10-Q states that the settlement required it to pay a penalty of $5.0 billion and to significantly enhance its privacy compliance and oversight practices.
facts.quote: required us to pay a penalty of $5.0 billion and to significantly enhance our practices and processes for privacy compliance and oversight

facts.claim: In July 2019 the FTC filed an administrative complaint against Cambridge Analytica and announced settlements with its former CEO Alexander Nix and app developer Aleksandr Kogan. The complaint alleged that users of the GSRApp were falsely told it would not collect their names or other identifiable information when it collected Facebook User IDs. Nix and Kogan consented to orders barring deceptive statements about data collection and requiring destruction of data collected through the app.
facts.quote: Kogan and Nix are barred from false or deceptive statements about the extent and purposes of their data collection and sharing

sources.title: FTC Sues Cambridge Analytica, Settles with Former CEO and App Developer

facts.claim: The Commission voted 5-0 to issue an opinion and final order against Cambridge Analytica in late 2019, finding that the company engaged in deceptive practices including in relation to its participation in the EU-US Privacy Shield, and ordering it to delete personal information collected through the GSRApp. Cambridge Analytica had filed for bankruptcy and did not settle. In December 2019 the FTC voted 5-0 to give final approval to the Nix and Kogan settlements.
facts.quote: The regulator voted 5-0 in favor of issuing the Opinion and Final Order

openQuestions: Site claim (Manufacturing Consent): 'The FTC fined Facebook $5 billion over privacy violations', tagged court, is supported by the FTC's July 24, 2019 press release; the penalty was a settlement with no admission of wrongdoing, which the site's wording does not say.

Site claim (Manufacturing Consent): 'harvested data from up to 87 million Facebook users' is attributed in press coverage to Facebook's own 2018 estimate; no FTC document stating the 87 million figure was located.
The full text of the FTC's opinion against Cambridge Analytica was not read; its date (reported as November 25, 2019) should be confirmed on ftc.gov.
